newsitem.title: UK: IGC 1996-97 coarse grain trade estimate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: IGC 1996-97 coarse grain trade estimate unchanged.

text.p: The International Grains Council on Thursday left its estimate for 1996-97 world coarse grains trade unchanged at 89 million tonnes, against 92 million in 1995-96.

The IGC cut its estimate of imports by far east Asian countries to 42.9 million tonnes from the previous 44.3 million, including cuts in estimates for Taiwan, down 400,000 tonnes to 5.9 million, and Japan, down 300,000 tonnes, to 20.5 million. China's estimated imports were lowered by 100,000 tonnes to 2.0 million tonnes.
Estimated EU imports were cut by 300,000 tonnes to 2.8 million, with reductions noted for Portugal and Spain.
It saw lower Mexican imports, down 200,000 tonnes to 5.6 million and reduced Brazilian imports by 300,000 tonnes to 600,000.

Rises were seen in central and eastern European states' imports, up 100,000 tonnes, the Baltic states, also up 100,000 tonnes, and Iran, up 200,000 tonnes. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
